name: Roubion
rock_type: altered basalt or microgabbro (no rock retained; tube holds atmosphere)
summary: The first coring attempt. The weathered rock crumbled into powder, so the sealed tube kept only Martian air. It was later left at the Three Forks depot.

name: Singita
campaign: Lac de Charmes (outside the crater rim)
summary: The first crystalline igneous sample collected outside Jezero crater. It may be among the oldest rocks in the collection, possibly older than Jezero itself.

citations.title: NASA Science blog: Newest Sample, Oldest Rock?
The Planetary Society: Mars rover samples what could be one of the oldest rocks on the Martian surface

notes: Not in Initial Reports vols. 1-5 or NASA's sample table yet, so it has no sample number or designation. The NASA blog dates a coring-bit image to Oct. 24, 2026 (sol 2018), 'shortly after coring'. The Planetary Society gives the same coring date. The outcrop or workspace name is not stated: an earlier abrasion at 'Badger Peak' was too hard to core, and Singita came from a neighbouring rock about 100 m away (latest abrasion 'Pumbe', sol 2011). NASA's table and the mid-2025 tube count (33 tubes by sol 1574) suggest no samples between Gallants and Singita, and the blog calls Singita the first sample in more than a year. Rock type comes from the blog's account of the gabbro search and the Planetary Society's 'crystalline igneous', not from a formal classification.
waypoint_at_sol_note: Last final ('y') waypoint in M20_waypoints.json at or before 'sol'; report_lat/report_lon come from the Mars 2020 Initial Report. There is no Initial Report coordinate for Singita, so this waypoint is the only position estimate.
